defects.note: importing net/http/pprof registers its handlers on http.DefaultServeMux in init, even when only pprof.Index is used on the debug mux; the public server has no Handler, so it serves DefaultServeMux and /debug/pprof/ is open to the internet next to the API. Set Handler: api on srv and never serve DefaultServeMux publicly

when the revocation list cannot be reached the error is logged and the request continues, so a revoked session works again whenever the list is down; a verifier error must answer 503, not fall through

the download route is registered without authed or member, unlike every other private route, so anyone without a session fetches an export; export IDs are sequential, so every export can be enumerated. Wrap the mux once with a public list instead of wrapping each route
the doc says the export goes to the member who made it, but nothing compares exp.Owner with the caller: once the route is wrapped, any signed-in user still downloads any other user's export by ID

member checked the org in the path, but the document is created in the org_id the body names: a member of o1 posting to /orgs/o1/docs with org_id o2 writes into o2. Drop the field and use r.PathValue("org")

the cache is keyed by document ID alone and a hit returns before the org comparison, so once anyone in o2 has read document 7, a member of o1 reads it through /orgs/o1/docs/7. Key on org and ID, or compare the org on every path
a document of another org answers 403 while a missing one answers 404, so a member learns which IDs exist elsewhere; a foreign ID answers exactly like a missing one
the export authorizes the org in the path once, then loads every requested ID with no org check: a member of o1 exports o2's documents by listing their IDs. Check each document's org against the path

strings.IndexByte returns -1 for a body with no newline, and d.Body[:-1] panics; render runs in its own goroutine, outside net/http's recover, so one export of a one-line document ends the whole process for every tenant

the Used check, AddMember, and MarkUsed take the lock separately, so concurrent redemptions of one code all pass the check and all join the org; spend the invite in one store call that reports whether this caller was the one

baits.note: a map lookup by the SHA-256 of a 128-bit random ID leaks nothing a timing attack can use; constant-time comparison is for comparing a secret with a guess, not for indexing by a hash

cookie sessions with no CSRF token are covered: CrossOriginProtection rejects a cross-origin state-changing request by Sec-Fetch-Site or Origin, and the __Host- cookie cannot be set by a sibling subdomain; a per-session token adds nothing here
